text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- KIDNAPPED BABY IS BACK IN MOTHER'S ARMS
Baby boy Rafael who was kidnapped on Sunday from a maternity ward in a Rio de Janeiro hospital 48 hours after being born has been found and returned to his parents.
Brazilian economists from the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) are forecasting an annual inflation rate of 11 percent this year which would be the lowest since 1950.
-- CARDOSO LETS MINISTERS BACK CANDIDATES IN SECOND ROUND

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has announced he would not openly back any of the candidates standing in the second round of municipal elections, but that his ministers were free to back any candidate they wanted.
-- NUMBER OF COUPLES OPTING FOR STERILIZATION GROWS
The number of Brazilian couples opting for sterilization as their method of contraception has grown more than 40 percent in the last 10 years.
-- MALAN IN FAVOR OF LONGER PRESIDENTIAL TERM

Finance minister Pedro Malan said a four year presidential term is very short. It should either be extended to five, six or even seven years or remain at four years with the possibility of re-election.
-- COURT BARS ELETROSUL FROM SACKING BLACK MAN

A Brazilian labor tribunal has barred electricity firm Eletrosul from firing a black technician until the court hands down its final ruling on the man's allegations that he was fired because he is black.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
